title: Composition of native compactly supported Weil direct images
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use the categories $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(-)$ and the actual equivariant derived operations $h^*,Rh_*,Rh_{0!}$ of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Let $V\xrightarrow{a}W\xrightarrow{b}T$ be separated quasi-compact locally finite-type morphisms of $k_0$-schemes, with $W$ and $T$ quasi-compact, quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] and locally of finite type over $k_0$. Then there is an isomorphism of functors on the native derived Weil categories
$$R(ba)_{0!}\cong Rb_{0!}\circ Ra_{0!}:\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(V)\longrightarrow\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(T).$$
The isomorphism is in the categories of Weil complexes, hence is equivariant.

source.place: nonempty_derivedLowerShriek_comp_iso, lines 187-200 (proof sorry); prop-functor-package clause 3. No absolute separatedness over k0 is assumed.

proof.text: Use the ambient native operations of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] and write $F_{(j,r)}=Rr_*J_j$. Quasi-compact locally finite-type maps are finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For an affine open $O$ of a target, take a finite affine cover $O_i$ of the inverse image under the second map; the inverse images of $O_i$ under the first map are quasi-compact and their finite union is the inverse image of $O$ under the composite. Thus $ba$ and $V$ over $k_0$ are quasi-compact. Separatedness and local finite type compose by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). The framework supplies chosen compactifications of $a,b,ba$.

proof.text: Write the chosen compactification of $b$ as $(i:W\hookrightarrow\overline W,q:\overline W\to T)$. Together with that of $ba$, [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower] supplies $z:V\hookrightarrow\overline V$, $p:\overline V\to\overline W$, $U=\overline V\times_{\overline W}W$, $t:U\hookrightarrow\overline V$, $p_W:U\to W$ and $s:V\hookrightarrow U$, with $ts=z$, $p_Ws=a$, $pt=ip_W$. Its $(s,p_W)$ and $(z,qp)$ compactify $a$ and $ba$. All are over $k_0$ via $T$ and finite type: the ambient schemes via the proper maps $q,p$ and $U$ via $p_W$, using finite type of proper maps and the same finite-cover composition argument as step 1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-native-weil-compatible-tower-calculation] to this tower, obtaining $F_{(z,qp)}\cong F_{(i,q)}F_{(s,p_W)}$ on bounded constructible inputs. By [lem-sf-native-weil-compactification-model-comparison], replace $F_{(z,qp)}$ and $F_{(s,p_W)}$ by the framework's chosen models for $ba$ and $a$; $(i,q)$ is already chosen for $b$. Whiskering these natural isomorphisms gives $R(ba)_{0!}\cong Rb_{0!}Ra_{0!}$ in the ambient native category.

proof.text: Both sides of the assembled comparison already come from the framework's chosen restricted functors on native Weil complexes, by the three model-comparison isomorphisms. Apply the preimageIso of whiskering by the fully faithful inclusion of native Weil complexes into their ambient derived category. This transports the natural isomorphism itself, with its inverse and naturality, into the full subcategory. No additional preservation-of-cohomology argument is required. All constituent maps lie in the native equivariant derived categories and hence respect Frobenius.

    [QuasiCompact f] [g.IsOver (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [IsSeparated g]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Z ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiCompact (Z ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiSeparated (Z ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] :
    Nonempty (derivedLowerShriek k₀ l (f ≫ g) ≅
      derivedLowerShriek k₀ l f ⋙ derivedLowerShriek k₀ l g)
